title: Justice and Impartiality
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Justice and impartiality means treating people with righteousness, fairness, and truth without favoritism. God forbids partiality and commands His people to defend what is right, especially for those easily mistreated.
summary: Justice and impartiality means treating people with righteousness, fairness, and truth without favoritism. God forbids partiality and commands His people to defend what is right, especially for those easily mistreated.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the righteous Judge who shows no sinful partiality. His kingdom exposes favoritism, honors truth, and calls His people to reflect God’s justice and mercy.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God shows no sinful partiality. He is righteous in all His ways, and He commands His people not to favor the rich over the poor, the powerful over the weak, or the familiar over the outsider.

Justice requires truth. Scripture forbids favoring either the poor or the great when judgment is required. Righteousness must not be distorted by status, fear, money, race, influence, or personal benefit.

God’s people are called to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves and to defend the rights of the needy. Justice is not a trend; it is part of walking humbly before God.

In Christ, favoritism is exposed as sin. The church must not rank people by wealth, ability, appearance, background, disability, or usefulness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Favoritism quietly destroys trust and contradicts the Gospel. When churches honor the impressive while neglecting the weak, they misrepresent the heart of God.

This doctrine calls believers to examine their assumptions, relationships, leadership, service, and care for the vulnerable under God’s righteous standard.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Reject favoritism in your speech, attention, leadership, and relationships. Treat people according to truth and dignity, not status or usefulness. Speak for those being mistreated and ask God to make your justice merciful, impartial, and obedient to Christ.
